dossier.architecture: Two-sided intake, transfer pivot and powerful launcher, with compact spring-deployed chain climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: REV modules with Vortex drive and custom TPU tread; team reports frequent wheel replacement.
subsystems.intake: Front/rear pickup feeds a central path; sensors stop the note and a low-friction plate supports it.
subsystems.transfer: Pivoting transfer preserves vertical compression into the launcher.
subsystems.scoring: Four Vortex-powered wheel groups and adjustable launch pivot; tested contact and compression govern geometry.
subsystems.endgame: Constant-force-spring deployment, powered retrieval and magnetic hook retention; side approach leaves harmony room.
subsystems.controls: AprilTag/odometry localization and shot lookup tables support scoring or passing into the protected amp-side area.

versions: Approximately eleven launcher iterations reported. TPU wheels replaced stock tread; hook magnet addressed inconsistent chain engagement.
dossier.analysis: Their role flexibility depended on deliberate pass landing zones, not merely being able to throw a note far. Wheel performance also carried a substantial consumable/service requirement.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.

context_documents.title: 2024-3005 · Contact geometry and fast wheel service both affect available scoring
context_documents.body:
# 2024-3005: Contact geometry and fast wheel service both affect available scoring

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Front/rear intake paths stage a note on low-friction support and feed a pivoting transfer. The launcher uses four Vortex-driven contact groups after tests with fewer contacts. The interview also discusses rapidly replaceable printed wheel components, reporting swaps in under a minute when a replacement is prepared.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says earlier arrangements did not provide sufficient contact and that additional roller power/placement emerged through testing. Serviceability was deliberately considered for playoff repair windows.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Motor count is the consequence of a contact requirement, not a standalone design target. Each contact must accelerate without deforming the note into a less repeatable state. Repair speed affects how much performance survives a tournament: a fast but fragile part may be viable only if replacement stock and access are designed at the same time.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare slip, note deformation and release speed across contact arrangements. Time an actual module replacement with match-ready tools and verify the resulting alignment.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
